steps.title: Domains and TLS
steps.subtitle: Host name only, such as pdf.example.com (no https:// in front). Stirling-PDF's SYSTEM_FRONTENDURL takes the full URL, https://pdf.example.com. For a name that is not public, turn Let's Encrypt off (see the README, Known limits).

steps.title: HTTP - Upload size
steps.subtitle: Largest PDF or request body to accept. BunkerWeb needs about 8 times this in memory, on top of its own use (see the README).

steps.title: HTTP - Long operations
steps.subtitle: How long BunkerWeb waits for a slow job such as OCR. Stirling-PDF stops jobs at 20 minutes.

steps.title: HTTP - Request rate
steps.subtitle: The web app sends one request per file, all at once: 100r/s lets a batch of files through.

steps.title: HTTP - API methods
steps.subtitle: Stirling-PDF uses PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS for storage, jobs and the desktop app.

steps.title: HTTP - Error messages
steps.subtitle: Pass Stirling-PDF's own error messages through so the web app and scripts can show them.

steps.title: Security - Real client address
steps.subtitle: Replace a client-sent X-Forwarded-For and drop Forwarded, so logs and limits see the real address.

steps.title: Security - Bad behavior status codes
steps.subtitle: Stirling-PDF answers 401 on every page load without a session: keep 401 and 400 out of the ban counter.

steps.title: Security - Phone camera
steps.subtitle: Let the phone scanner page ask for the camera (QR upload from a phone). If you do not use it, set the camera entry to camera=() (type it, do not clear the field).

steps.title: Security - Sign-in with authentik (optional)
steps.subtitle: Leave empty to skip. To require an authentik sign-in first, fill REVERSE_PROXY_HOST_1, REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_REQUEST and REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_REQUEST_SIGNIN_URL as the README shows.

steps.title: Security - Review CRS exclusions
steps.subtitle: Skip injection rules for the Automate pipeline JSON and saved signature images, and the file-name rule for uploads under /api/v1/.
